title: Polesie — Land of Marshes and Cranes
lead: Wetlands, cranes, and wooden educational trails leading through an extraordinary marsh ecosystem. Slow travel through Polesie Lubelskie.
body:
Why Polesie, differently

Polesie is one of the most mysterious corners of Poland, where land and water form a fascinating mosaic. It is a land where the rhythm of life is set by the rise and fall of marsh waters. Polesie National Park — one of the youngest in Poland (established in 1990) — protects a fragment of this unique ecosystem, home to many rare species of plants and animals.

Slow travel through Polesie is a celebration of silence and attention. Instead of rushing from attraction to attraction, sit on an observation tower, look at the marshes, listen to the call of cranes. A walk through peat bogs is an experience that teaches patience — the longer you are in this landscape, the more details you notice: rare plants, interesting birds, animal tracks. Polesie is a land that rewards those who slow down — and reminds us that we are only part of a larger, fascinating ecosystem.

What to see

Polesie National Park splits into several parts: the strict reserve (centre), the Education Centre in Urszulin, educational trails, observation towers. Two to three days are best to visit.

Trails and observation towers

  • Dąb Dominik Trail — the most interesting route in the park. A wooden boardwalk leads through peat bogs and lets you see this extraordinary ecosystem up close. Worth it for contact with nature.
  • Spławy Trail — a route through peat bogs and marsh forests, with viewpoints. Worth it for lesser-known views.
  • Observation tower over Lake Łukie — a tower with a view over the lake and marshes. Worth it for birdwatching.
  • Tower in Urszulin — a tower at the Education Centre, with a panorama of the park. Worth it for views.
  • Żółw Trail — a route through European pond turtle habitats, with educational boards.

Karst lakes and fauna

  • Lake Łukie — the largest karst lake in the park, with clean water and an interesting ecosystem. Worth a walk.
  • Lake Moszne — a peat bog lake with unique vegetation. Worth it for birdwatching.
  • European pond turtle — the park's symbol, one of the most endangered reptiles in Poland. Look out for it on the trails.
  • Cranes and waterfowl — the park is a paradise for birds. In spring and autumn you can hear the call of cranes.
  • Beavers — inhabit the park's rivers and canals, building dams and lodges. Worth it for observation.

Education Centre and surroundings

  • Education Centre in Urszulin — the park museum, with an exhibition about the nature of Polesie. Worth it for context.
  • Wola Uhruska — a village with a wooden Orthodox church, ~15 km from Urszulin. Worth it for architecture.
  • Włodawa — a small town with a Baroque synagogue and Orthodox church, ~30 km from the park. Worth it for history and architecture.
  • Chełm — a town with chalk hills, ~40 km from the park. Worth it for architecture.
  • Sobibór — a former extermination camp, ~10 km from the park. Worth it for history.

When to go

  • May and June — the best time for birdwatchers. Birds in full migration, marshes full of life. Come with binoculars.
  • September and October — second bird peak. Autumn migrations, autumn colours on the marshes. Worth it for birdwatchers.
  • July and August — warm days but fewer birds. Mosquitoes troublesome — bring repellent.
  • November–March — winter on the marshes can be harsh, but quiet. Worth it for those who seek solitude.

Getting there

  • By car: ~1 hour from Lublin (DK82), ~40 minutes from Chełm, ~3.5 hours from Warsaw (S17 and DK82).
  • By train: station in Chełm or Włodawa (~30 km from the park), with connections from Lublin (~1.5 hours), Warsaw (~4 hours).
  • By bus: PKS and private operators from Lublin and Chełm to Urszulin.

Public transport in the region is sparse — a car makes moving between attractions much easier.

How much time you need

A weekend (2 days) is the minimum — Dąb Dominik and Spławy trails, observation towers, birdwatching.

Three days is realistic for a first visit. One day for trails and towers, one for birdwatching, one for Włodawa and surroundings.

A week lets you explore the whole Polesie — park, surroundings, Włodawa, Chełm and other regional attractions.

What to eat and where to sleep

  • Lublin cuisine — Lublin cebularz, pierogi with bryndza, krupnik. Worth trying in local inns.
  • Lake fish — pike, bream, tench. Smoked or fried.
  • Mushrooms — in season (August–October) local dishes with mushrooms.
  • Beer from a local brewery — several craft breweries in the region.
  • Coffee and cake — Urszulin and Włodawa have several good cafés.
  • Korycin cheeses — smoked and aged, available in local shops.

Accommodation: Urszulin (closest to the park, smaller choice), Włodawa (~30 km, more options), Chełm (~40 km, more options), agritourism farms in villages around the park (quiet, cheaper), Lublin (~60 km, more options).

Practical tips

  • Bookings — book campsites and agritourism farms around the park in advance in season.
  • Binoculars — without binoculars you will not see most birds. Rent or buy before your trip.
  • Mosquitoes and ticks — marshes are paradise for mosquitoes and ticks. Repellent and mosquito net — essential.
  • Shoes — sturdy shoes (rubber boots okay) are essential on trails. Routes may be wet.
  • Water and food — no food points on trails. Bring your own.
  • Signal — good in Urszulin and Włodawa, weaker deep in the park.
  • PPN tickets — required on trails in Polesie National Park. Buy online or at entry kiosks.
tip: Visit Polesie in May — it is the best month for birdwatching. The peat bogs are full of life then, and the trails are not yet crowded.
